label: Stream
description: Stream a bus to the caller of this run, one chunk per message, until the bus closes. Behind a Route the response body streams as the bus flows (`sse` for a browser's EventSource and LLM-style clients, `ndjson` for a script reading lines, `raw` for the payloads as they are) and ends when the bus closes. Behind a Socket each message is one socket message and the socket stays open. Wire an LLM Stream's bus in to stream a reply as it is generated, or a Postgres: Watch query's to keep a page live. A stored file inside a message goes out as `{ url, mimeType, filename, sizeBytes }`, a link the caller can fetch.

inputs.name: bus
inputs.description: The live bus to stream: every message on it, in order, from the earliest still buffered; the bus closing ends the stream.

inputs.name: first
inputs.description: A value sent ahead of the bus, framed exactly like the messages behind it. This is the header every streaming API has: an id, the row that was just created, a session token, and then the feed. Leave it off and the response is the bus alone.

inputs.name: format
inputs.label: Format
inputs.description: How each message is framed on an HTTP body (ignored on a socket, where a message is a frame). `raw`: the payload as-is, no separator. `ndjson`: one JSON value per line. `sse`: server-sent events, `data:` lines and a blank line per message.

inputs.name: answerAs
inputs.label: Answer as
inputs.description: The shape of each `raw` message (and of the socket's frames). Empty (default) uses the trigger's own `dataType`. Set it when what goes out differs from what came in.

inputs.name: status
inputs.label: Status
inputs.description: The HTTP status of the response (Route only).

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Extra response headers by name (Route only). A content-type here overrides the one the format implies.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires true once the bus closed and the last chunk was handed to the caller.

then.message: Stream '{id}' answers nobody: no trigger with a live caller (a Route, a Socket) starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
Stream '{id}' runs after {with}, which already sent the response's head to the HTTP caller, so this stream can never go out. Send everything through one Stream, and end the exchange with a Close.
